title: Fix MacOS compile error by updating Immutable buffer type
body:
Fixed this MacOS compilation error by changing the `ImmutableBuffer` type from `std::shared_ptr<char[]>` to `std::shared_ptr<char>` with an appropriate array deleter. 

This resolves the type compatibility issue between `char (*)[]` and the required const char* return type for the data() method.
author: douenergy

comments.body:
After running `make test_debug_unit `

two unit test will failed. 

1. test_set_extension_config.cpp's test case `Test on changing extension config change default cache dir path setting`

```
SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free file_open_flags.hpp:111 in duckdb::FileOpenFlags::GetFlagsInternal() const
```

2. test_exclusive_multi_lru_cache.cpp's test case  `Put items with the same key`

```
SUMMARY: AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free string:1682 in std::__1::basic_string<char, std::__1::char_traits<char>, std::__1::allocator<char>>::__is_long[abi:v160006]() const
```
@douenergy could you please paste the **error message for compilation failure** in PR description?

@dentiny  The original compile error messenge 

```
/duck-read-cache-fs/src/utils/include/immutable_buffer.hpp:23:38: error: no matching constructor for initialization of 'std::shared_ptr<char[]>'
        ImmutableBuffer(std::size_t size) : buffer(new char[size]), buf_size(size) {
                                            ^      ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
```

```
/duck-read-cache-fs/src/utils/include/immutable_buffer.hpp:33:10: error: cannot initialize return object of type 'const char *' with an rvalue of type 'element_type *' (aka 'char (*)[]')
                return buffer.get();
                       ^~~~~~~~~~~~
```

OK I could reproduce on my local macos; I think the issue is, shared pointer of array is a C++17 feature, which is not supported by all stdlib implementation.

I'll revert related PRs; meanwhile could you please close the PR? Thanks.
